source_version: Probability on Trees and Networks, author paperback version 2026-08-19

read_scope.pixel_inspection_reason: Three independent image probes in this session returned image data with no readable text conclusion, so pixel viewing cannot serve as assertable evidence. Transcription fidelity below rests on the PDF text layer of both the reader and the source, checked with four deterministic instruments.

coverage_checks.detail: Editorial context section names every reprinted page with both physical and printed folios; the eight locator lines in the source are reproduced, and no reprinted passage is left unattributed.

Primary statement is contained verbatim in the source text layer of physical p. 289 (word coverage 0.92 under the strict measure and exact letter-skeleton containment, so the residue is spacing in the display formula only). The identical statement, also printed on physical p. 278, was likewise found verbatim there.

Both solutions of the author Comment are contained verbatim: Solution 1 (coverage 1.0), Solution 2 opening (1.0), the recursion sentence (1.0), the Fekete application (0.92 with exact skeleton containment), and the even-k close (1.0).

Proposition 6.6 with (6.12)-(6.15), the self-adjointness computation, and both sentences of the Taylor-Lay footnote are contained verbatim; the irreducibility sentence begins physical p. 202 and matches at coverage 1.0 there.
Fekete's lemma lead, the subadditivity definition, and Exercise 3.9 parts (a)-(c) are contained verbatim on physical p. 102; Comment 3.9 parts (a)-(c) are contained verbatim on physical p. 622.

claim_level_measure.residual_difference_explained: The single near_verbatim passage (physical p. 201, word coverage 0.85) reads 'at most 1. As the reader should recall from the theory of Markov chains ...'. In the source, the boxed in-text Exercise 6.6 ('Prove that ||P||_pi <= 1') is set between 'at most 1.' and 'As the reader should recall', so the source text layer interleaves it. The reader correctly reproduces the two author sentences and correctly places Exercise 6.6 as reprinted context. The difference is a source-layout insertion, not a reader alteration.

preserved_literal_source_notation: The displayed equation numbering (6.12), (6.13), (6.14), (6.15) is preserved as printed.
The exercise label '7.10.' inside the Comment ('7.10. Solution 1.') is preserved, matching the source's own labelling.
The source's 'lim sup' and 'lim' are kept distinct wherever the source distinguishes them.
The Taylor-Lay citation is preserved with its theorem number VI.3.3.

errata_handling.finding: The separate errata sheet dated 19 August 2026 contains no entry for Chapter 7; accordingly no revision is applied anywhere in this reader, and no printed text here is altered. No source mathematics is repaired or independently certified.

limitations: No pixel inspection of any page was performed in this session; the conclusion rests on text layers and geometric measurement only.

The PDF text layer of this source has three systematic artefacts that any naive substring test will misread: (a) Latin ligatures are decomposed ('de ned', 'su ces', 'satis es', 'in nite', ' rst', 'nition', 'in mum', 'di cult'); (b) the sans-serif V used for the vertex set is dropped from the text layer ('l2( ,' where the reader prints 'l2(V, pi)'); (c) non-breaking spaces glue tokens ('<an>of', '<= r <= m -1;'). The final instrument expands ligature code points and compares letter skeletons, which removes (a) and (b) without weakening the test.

Text-layer extraction flattens super- and subscripts, so exponent and index placement is not verified by these instruments; it is verified only insofar as LaTeX produced it and latexmk reported no error.
